reply:
That changes it. PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct from each other in UNIQUE constraints, so multiple NULLs can coexist. The second NULL does not violate the constraint.

This is PostgreSQL-specific. SQL Server treats NULLs as equal for UNIQUE purposes and blocks the second NULL. Other databases (Oracle, MySQL, SQLite) behave like Postgres—allowing multiple NULLs.

My initial answer conflated the SQL standard (NULL ≠ NULL) with how each engine enforces UNIQUE. PostgreSQL follows the standard here; SQL Server does not.

grade.note: Reply correctly reverses position, agrees NULLs are distinct in Postgres UNIQUE, and explains cross-DB differences.
